title: My Factory: ideas for automating your AI dev workflow
author: dr0idattack137
selftext:
I've been running a setup where I mostly just write issues and play the builds, and a crew of AI agents does the rest. The first thing it's building is a mobile game for iOS (released) and Android (inflight) Diagram above, but here's the plain version.

**The basic flow**

1. I write an issue in the backlog app.
2. A dispatcher picks it up and starts one agent session for that issue.
3. A router decides who should build it. A small local model looks at the kind of work and how hard it is, and decides in about a second. If it isn't sure, it asks a small cloud model.
4. A builder writes the code, tests, art, or sound. I have three cloud agent vendors plus a local GPU model, each with small, mid, and top tiers.
5. A reviewer from a *different* vendor checks the pull request. It can't see the builder's reasoning, only the code. No agent ever reviews its own work.
6. If the review passes, it auto-merges as long as main is green.
7. It goes to a simulator or a TestFlight / Android test, and I play it.

**When things go wrong (which is most of the interesting part)**

* **Failed review:** the findings go back to the builder for a fix round.
* **Fix rounds stall:** an arbiter steps in. It's a top-tier model with read-only access. It either merges and files follow-up issues, or sends the work back.
* **Main goes red:** every new main runs simulator tests. A red build files an urgent repair issue, and an agent picks it up like any other issue. A suspected flaky test gets one rerun. There's also a nightly game balance run.
* **A vendor hits a quota or hangs:** a "healer" runs every 2 minutes. It wakes stalled sessions, retries errors, and reroutes work to another vendor. If nobody else can take it, the work waits until the limit resets.

The main idea is that every failure comes back as a new backlog issue. Nothing just dies quietly.

**Where I still come in**  
Imagination, ideas. Anything that changes how the game looks or sounds waits for me to approve. Everything else merges when tests pass. I get a live status page and a daily email.

**A few things I learned**

* Cross-vendor review catches a lot more than same-model review. Models are oddly forgiving of their own style of mistakes.
* Routing by quota left and first-review pass rate works better than always picking the "best" model.
* Rework needs a limit. Without the arbiter, two agents would happily argue forever.
* I log every routing or model change as a dated decision, with the data behind it and an undo step. That saved me more than once.

Happy to answer questions about any part of it.

(First game shipped with it is Riveting: pachinko roguelike in the iOS App Store.)
